title: Water Management and Conservation
desc: Measure, save and manage water at home, farm, school or business, with leak checks, rainwater, reuse and fair sharing.
outcomes: Explain the water cycle and local water risks.
Do a water audit and leak test.
Judge quality, safety and cost of reuse.
Write a water-saving plan with targets.
task: Audit water use at one site, plan savings, design a rainwater or reuse option and set a measurable target.
condition: A real site or a practice case, a bucket and timer or meter, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Audit lists all uses in litres; leak test is documented; savings and payback are calculated; water safety rules are stated; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Facility managers, farmers, school staff, residents, community groups.
evidence: audit sheet, leak test record, plan, target
modules: A town cuts supply in summer; households store water.
Read the meter at the same time daily.
List uses: taps, toilets, showers, cleaning, irrigation.
Convert to litres per day per person.
A home uses 180 L per person per day.
Night meter test; dye test for toilets.
A drip per second wastes thousands of litres a year.
A toilet leak is found with food dye and repaired.
Aerators, efficient flushes, full loads, shorter showers.
Roof area x rainfall x efficiency = litres.
First-flush diverter, filter and covered tank.
100 m2 roof and 800 mm rain gives about 64,000 L a year.
Grey water from basins can irrigate with care.
Avoid contact with edible leaves where unsafe.
A school sets a 20% cut in one year.
quiz: Litres per person per day?
Total use / people / days. (Covered in module 1: Water cycle and risk. To pass that module: Sources named.)
Night meter test?
No use but meter moves means a leak. (Covered in module 2: Water audit. To pass that module: Table complete.)
Rainwater formula?
Area x rain x efficiency. (Covered in module 3: Finding leaks. To pass that module: Result recorded.)
Safe grey water use?
Irrigation of non-edible plants. (Covered in module 4: Saving at the tap. To pass that module: Savings estimated.)
Aerator benefit?
Reduces flow. (Covered in module 5: Rainwater harvesting. To pass that module: Calculation correct.)
Why first flush?
Removes dirt. (Covered in module 6: Reuse and quality. To pass that module: Rules clear.)
Mulch use?
Keeps moisture. (Covered in module 7: Irrigation and farming. To pass that module: Plan complete.)
Drinking water rule?
Treat and test. (Covered in module 8: Plan and target. To pass that module: Target measurable.)
Why meters?
To measure savings. (Covered in module 8: Plan and target. To pass that module: Target measurable.)
Why share plan?
Community buy-in. (Covered in module 8: Plan and target. To pass that module: Target measurable.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: plastic alternatives, greenhouse gas auditing, vertical farming.
local: Water rights, rainwater and reuse rules differ by place.
ladder: Water cycle and risk

L1: learner can name water sources. Focus module: Water cycle and risk (Understand, 3 h). Where water comes from. Key points: Rain, rivers, groundwater, storage. Droughts, floods and quality problems. Know your supply and rules.

Teach: open with the worked example. A town cuts supply in summer; households store water. Then set the activity: Describe your supply. Mark against the standard: Sources named. Check at this level: Litres per person per day? Model answer: Total use / people / days. Cycle.
Water audit

L2: learner knows leak basics. Focus module: Water audit (Apply, 5 h). Measure first. Key points: Read the meter at the same time daily. List uses: taps, toilets, showers, cleaning, irrigation. Convert to litres per day per person.

Teach: open with the worked example. A home uses 180 L per person per day. Then set the activity: Do an audit. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: Night meter test? Model answer: No use but meter moves means a leak. Leaks.
Finding leaks

L3: learner can audit. Focus module: Finding leaks (Apply, 4 h). Small drips cost a lot. Key points: Night meter test; dye test for toilets. A drip per second wastes thousands of litres a year. Fix quickly.

Teach: open with the worked example. A toilet leak is found with food dye and repaired. Then set the activity: Run a leak test. Mark against the standard: Result recorded. Check at this level: Rainwater formula? Model answer: Area x rain x efficiency. Audit.
Saving at the tap
L4: learner can fix and save. Focus module: Saving at the tap (Analyse, 4 h). Cheap measures. Key points: Aerators, efficient flushes, full loads, shorter showers. Behaviour and signs. Track savings.

Teach: open with the worked example. Aerators save 25% at taps. Then set the activity: Choose five measures. Mark against the standard: Savings estimated. Check at this level: Safe grey water use? Model answer: Irrigation of non-edible plants. Measures.
Rainwater harvesting

L5: learner can design rainwater. Focus module: Rainwater harvesting (Create, 5 h). Catch and store. Key points: Roof area x rainfall x efficiency = litres. First-flush diverter, filter and covered tank. Use for non-drinking unless treated.

Teach: open with the worked example. 100 m2 roof and 800 mm rain gives about 64,000 L a year. Then set the activity: Design a system. Mark against the standard: Calculation correct. Check at this level: Aerator benefit? Model answer: Reduces flow. Design.
Irrigation and farming
L6: learner can lead a plan. Focus module: Irrigation and farming (Apply, 3 h). Use less, grow more. Key points: Drip lines, mulching, timing. Soil moisture checks. Crop choice for local rain.

Teach: open with the worked example. Drip cuts water by 40%. Then set the activity: Plan a plot. Mark against the standard: Plan complete. Check at this level: Why first flush? Model answer: Removes dirt. Lead.
Plan and target
L7: learner can audit others. Focus module: Plan and target (Create, 4 h). Make it stick. Key points: Targets, owners, dates. Report monthly. Share with the community.

Teach: open with the worked example. A school sets a 20% cut in one year. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Mark against the standard: Target measurable. Check at this level: Mulch use? Model answer: Keeps moisture. Peer audit.
